newsitem.title: INDIA: India fertiliser firm to expand output by March 97.
newsitem.headline: India fertiliser firm to expand output by March 97.

text.p: Production at India's Madras Fertilisers will increase by 50 percent to 1.05 million tonnes per annum by end March 1997 after the completion of an ongoing expansion programme, the company said on Friday.

"The last of the major equipment is expected to reach the site within the next two to three weeks and the hook-up with the existing production line is slated to commence by end January 1997," Madras Fertilisers said in a statement.
"As per current estimates, the expanded capacity would be ready for commissioning by end March 1997."
Madras Fertilisers, which manufactures chemical fertilisers, reported a turnover of 6.86 billion rupees in 1995/96 (April-March) and a net profit of 210.7 million, the statement said.

The company was incorporated in 1966 as a joint venture between the Indian government with a 51 percent equity stake, and AMOCO India Inc. holding the balance. AMOCO India Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of Standard Oil Company of the U.S.

Subsequently AMOCO divested their shares to the Indian government and the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), a state-owned Iranian firm. The Indian government currently holds 69.78 percent of the equity and the balance is held by NIOC.
